title: The corrected two-vector carrier can select Lorentz symmetry only under a rank-one alignment condition

claim.statement: One timelike SO(2,3) vector-5 can act as a MacDowell-Mansouri compensator with SO(1,3) stabilizer, but two generic independent vector-5 expectation values overbreak the symmetry; the corrected 2x5 carrier must align to rank one in multiplicity space.
claim.significance: This supplies a concrete route from the programme's carrier representation to an Einstein-Cartan-type action, while converting the second vector copy into a sharp vacuum-alignment constraint.

results.alignmentCondition: The two vector-5 VEVs must be parallel as SO(2,3) vectors, so the 2x5 expectation matrix has multiplicity-space rank one.

interpretation: The vector-5 carrier correction is not merely bookkeeping: it contains the correct compensator representation for selecting Lorentz symmetry.
The second copy can be a radial/flavour partner only if the potential aligns it with the first; a generic two-vector vacuum leaves a three-dimensional subgroup.
This route explains how Spin(2,3) geometry could organize gravity without identifying the finite adjoint zero-form with the gauge connection.
The cosmological and Einstein-Hilbert coefficients are linked by the AdS scale in the minimal action.
falsifiers: A proposed vacuum with two nonparallel vector-5 VEVs fails the six-dimensional Lorentz-stabilizer requirement.
A viable model must derive, not assume, timelike nonzero norm and rank-one alignment.
The compensator does not supply the independent one-form connection or its quantum dynamics.
nextBranches: Project candidate-48 vacuum data into the two vector-5 multiplicity space and test rank-one alignment directly.
